placement.position_note: Interpretive placement on a GENERATED lot, not a recovered parcel. The lot geometry is the K7 plat module's — this project has never read Thompson's numbering off a sheet, and the side lot lines and the alley are conjectural even where the block face is not. The building stands 4.0 m back from its street edge, which is a typology for the period and not a measurement of this lot. The whole footprint — not its centre — is tested against the platted street corridors, against its own lot lines and against every other footprint in the dataset, so no invented building of this parcel stands in the roadway; clearing the roadway is not the same as standing on a recovered lot.

persons.name: Charles H. Bartlett
persons.note: PROJECTED RESIDENT. Documented in Chicago post-office evidence but not independently corroborated strongly enough for attested circa-1835 residence. KNOWN ONLY FROM THE POST OFFICE, IN ONE RETURN. The papers print '‘Bartlett, Charles H,' in a single return of letters uncalled-for at the Chicago post office — the Democrat of 20 May 1835, column 13 — dated 1835-05-20. Nothing else in the corpus names this person: no trade, no street, no household, no arrival, so every other claim here is written unattested in its own block. WHAT THAT IS WORTH: a correspondent believed a person of this name reachable at Chicago on that date, and nothing further — not that they lived here, kept a trade here, or were here on 1 July 1835. It is the weakest evidence this project accepts for a resident, and a source placing them elsewhere retires the record. THE ARGUMENT EVERY RECORD OF THIS KIND SHARES is written once instead of once per file: the ruling of 2026-08-30 and what it cost the town (docs/LIBERTIES.md L214), the refusals and the transcription standard behind the reading (tools/mint_letter_list_residents.py). No figure is drawn (L1).

persons.name: C. George
persons.note: A DOCUMENTED PERSON, AND NOTHING ELSE IS CLAIMED. The papers name 'C. GEORGE' and give the trade; they do not say where this household lived, who else was in it, or when it came. So the record around this person carries nothing but the person: no dwelling, no division, no family, each written as unattested in its own block rather than filled in from the shape of the rest of the town. Cited at the Democrat of 5 November 1834, column 9. THE TOWN NEVER INVENTED A ROOF FOR THIS TRADE. The occupation census raised reconstructed households for the trades a town of 3,265 people needed and could not document; `baker` was not one of them, which is why this person could only ever be ADDED and never seated on an existing record — data/research/newspapers/register_1835.json calls it `new_resident` for exactly that reason. No figure is drawn (docs/LIBERTIES.md L1). READ THROUGH A TRANSCRIPTION, not a scan: the owner's ruling of 2026-08-28 grades a transcription-mediated reading as documented, and the source record for the run states that standard and its limits. A scan read that confirms or corrects the name upgrades this entry.

persons.name: Samuel E. Toby
persons.note: GRADED BY THE OWNER'S RATIFIED LADDER — rule G3, applied 2026-09-04. This identity is inferred because that rung fired on the civic and press rows recorded on this card, which the resident-research corpus does not read. This programme's letter-list rule of 2026-09-02 would call it a projected resident on the absence of a research row; it is superseded here, and a no-find in one corpus is not a finding about another (T-0822). KNOWN ONLY FROM THE POST OFFICE, IN ONE RETURN PRINTED THREE TIMES. The return of letters uncalled-for at the Chicago post office on 1 July 1834 was set three times in the Chicago Democrat — 1834-07-02 p3 c2, 1834-07-09 p1 c2 and 1834-07-16 p1 c2 — and two of those settings print 'samuel E. Toby' where the middle one prints 'samuel. Toby' and sets no middle initial at all. THE OWNER RULED ON 2026-09-24 (T-1528) that a present initial may absorb an ABSENT one at the same entry of the same list, bounded exactly as T-0392's unread-initial ruling was, and the gazetteer now keys this person on 'Samuel E. Toby' — the reading that carries every letter a printing set, which tools/compile_gazetteer.py refuses to let a merge discard. THIS CARD WEARS THAT READING (T-1561). It displayed 'Samuel. Toby' until then, which is the ABSORBED side: after the merge, nothing this record cites read the name that way, and the surviving reading was sitting in this card's own press_evidence row. THE ID DOES NOT MOVE WITH THE NAME — `toby_samuel` is a handle every crosswalk cites and not a claim (rule N5, T-1139), and the family name it was minted off is the one the card still reads. AND THE FIELD NOW FOLLOWS THE MERGED RECORD (T-1562). `letter_list_returns` is one date PER RETURN and not per printing, so three impressions of the 1 July 1834 return put ONE date in it, and it is the first printing that carries the name: 1834-07-02. It held the 1834-07-09 impression until then, which was neither the first printing nor the last but the issue one extraction crop reached. Reading the last printing in instead would date the evidence by a compositor's re-run; carrying both ends would say the office held letters for this man in two separate returns, which is the strongest thing a letter list can say about residence and is not what happened. THE ARRIVAL BLOCK DID NOT MOVE — it is dated by the return and never by the impression (T-0425), so it read 1834-07-01 while the earliest printing behind the name was still eight days late, and it reads 1834-07-01 now. Nothing else in the corpus names this person: no trade, no street, no household, no arrival, so every other claim here is written unattested in its own block. WHAT THAT IS WORTH: a correspondent believed a person of this name reachable at Chicago on that date, and nothing further — not that they lived here, kept a trade here, or were here on 1 July 1835. It is the weakest evidence this project accepts for a resident, and a source placing them elsewhere retires the record. No figure is drawn (L1).

citations.citation: Chicago · July 1835: Building Inventory and Architectural Reconstruction Specification. Prepared for Kevin Haas, August 2026.
what_it_supplies: A 665-roof production target with independently reconcilable group, district, level, and construction totals.
Thirty-five architectural family definitions with dimensional and massing bands.
District character, spacing, variation, finish, and chronology constraints for a July 1835 reconstruction.
A required distinction between named documentary landmarks and anonymous inferred infill.
what_it_does_not_supply: A surviving July 1835 building census or parcel-by-parcel roof register.
Exact locations, dimensions, appearance, occupants, or construction dates for anonymous roofs.
Authority to replace stronger building-specific evidence already represented in the dataset.

research_note: RECONSTRUCTED / GENERATED, NOT AN ATTESTED NAMED BUILDING. The block, its scheduled roof count and its family mix follow the 665-roof programme; exact presence, lot, position, footprint, finish and instance-level form are interpretive.

fabric_basis.words: new-sawn clapboard on a balloon frame, 12-over-12 sash of 6 × 8 in glass, plain corner boards and a stoop, under a new roof — a one-room frame cottage, new-built (rule F-T: a tradesman's by its type)
